mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement uses the phrase 'difference between' to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between Alice and Bob' as |Alice - Bob| (absolute value) instead of Alice - Bob.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more than B' (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N, using the exact order and sign of N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct comparison that states one person has a certain number more (or fewer) than another.
mathgap.example: Reversing the equation to B = A + N for 'A has N more than B'.

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When processing a transfer statement, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, using the current counts at that point.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form 'X gives N items to Y' appears.
mathgap.example: Delaying the transfer until after all other statements, thus using outdated counts for the giver and receiver.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When encountering a direct count statement, set the person's count to the given number at that point, overwriting any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says 'Person has N items'.
mathgap.example: Treating a later direct count as an initial value and ignoring earlier updates that already changed the person's count.

mathgap.title: Preserve Difference Order
mathgap.principle: When equating a 'has more than' difference to a 'difference between' two persons, preserve the order of subtraction on both sides (i.e., X - Y = A - B).
mathgap.when_to_apply: In statements that set a 'more than' difference equal to another difference.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between A and B' as B - A, thereby reversing the intended order.

mathgap.title: Temporal Evaluation of Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: When evaluating a relational statement, use the current counts of the persons at that point in the text, reflecting any prior transfers or updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational equation refers to persons whose counts may have changed earlier in the sequence.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a later relational statement after a transfer has already altered that count.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When encountering a conditional transfer, first evaluate the condition using the current counts, and only apply the transfer if the condition holds.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement includes a condition such as 'if X has at least N items, X gives N to Y'.
mathgap.example: Applying the transfer without checking the condition, leading to an impossible negative count for the giver.

mathgap.title: Combined Sum Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement gives a combined total for several persons, interpret it as the sum of those persons' counts equals the given total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering phrasing like 'The total number of items that A, B, and C have is N'.
mathgap.example: Treating the combined total as each person having N items individually, rather than the sum of their counts.

mathgap.title: Split Equally Among Recipients (Additive)
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among recipients, set the donor's count to 0 and add an equal share to each recipient.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'Person gives all their items equally to X and Y' or similar.
mathgap.example: Leaving the donor's count unchanged after the split, instead of setting it to zero.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative Increase Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X that Y has increases by p/q times', treat it as a scaling operation: multiply Y's current count by the factor p/q (do not add p/q times the count).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering phrasing like 'increases by N times' or 'increases by a fraction times'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'increases by 8/7 times' as adding 8/7 of the current count (resulting in a factor of 15/7) instead of multiplying by 8/7.

mathgap.description: Interpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to treating 'difference' as a magnitude, forgetting that the order of names determines the sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order as stated and compute X - Y, not |X - Y|.

mathgap.description: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their sequential effect.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model tends to batch updates, treating transfers as a separate phase rather than as they appear.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it is encountered, updating both giver and receiver before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming 'A has N more than B' implies A > B and discarding solutions where the computed difference is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing suggests a positive difference, leading the model to reject equations that yield a negative result.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate 'A has N more than B' directly to A = B + N; the sign of N encodes the direction, and the equation may be valid even if N is negative.

mathgap.description: Treating a direct count statement as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct assignments as fixed facts rather than mutable state that can change via later transfers.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, set the count at that point, but allow later transfer statements to modify it.

mathgap.description: Evaluating relational statements using outdated counts (e.g., initial values) instead of the current counts after prior statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may keep a snapshot of counts from the start and fail to incorporate earlier updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always use the most recent values of all persons when processing a relational statement, reflecting any prior transfers or assignments.
